  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run

      # gh-1738: activate is its own step so the Quality gates step below
      # can run for docs-only / app-zone-only PRs too — the similarity
      # corpus lives in docs/, prompts/, flutter_app/ and packages/, and
      # a diff confined there must reach the gate pre-merge (it routes

      - name: Activate crap4dart (pinned)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          # crap4dart#3/#4 (2026-10-15): >=0.14.2 — the broken_goldens

          # boxes, solid glyph runs); the configs now rely on 0.14.2

          # gh-1738: >=0.15.0 — the similarity gate (file-level
          # near-duplicates over md+dart), wired into crap4dart.yaml.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.15.0 <0.16.0"

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # crap4dart activated (pinned) in the step above.
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        # gh-1738: + docs/app — the similarity gate scans the whole tree
        # (docs/, prompts/, flutter_app/, packages/ included); no project

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.docs == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800

      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)

# Changelog

## 0.29.0 — 2026-10-30

- New `non_null_assertion` gate (warning severity by default): flags every non-null assertion — the postfix `!` operator (`x!`, `map['k']!`, chains `a!.b!`) and the null-assert pattern (`case var x!`). A bang crashes on unexpected null where the null-safe alternatives carry the same intent with a readable check: `?.`/`??` (the check-then-bang ternary `E != null ? E!.m() : f` collapses to `E?.m() ?? f`; getters and record fields do not promote, so the collapse is the only bang-free form) and the null-check pattern (`case var x?`). `!=`, logical-not `!x`, `++`/`--`, `?.` and `??` are not flagged. Zero thresholds; every violation carries the file and line of the `!` token. Existing codebases adopt via baseline ratchet (`check --save-baseline`) or warning severity. Independently validated by DCM's `avoid-non-null-assertion`.

## 0.28.0 — 2026-10-29

- New `collapsible_flow` gate (warning severity by default): flags control-flow nesting that a semantics-preserving mechanical rewrite can flatten. Three checks: collapsible `if (a) { if (b) X }` merges into `if (a && b) X` (short-circuit preserves order — always equivalent, pattern `case` conditions never merge); redundant `else` after an always-exiting then-branch dedents (an inner `if` without `else` never counts as exiting — control falls through; `switch` bodies are not analyzed for case fall-through); and an `else if` after an always-exiting then is a chain-flattening hint (guard sequence or dispatch table — report-only). Independently validated by DCM's `avoid-collapsible-if`/`avoid-redundant-else`. Dogfooded: the gate's first self-scan found a collapsible if inside the `identical_branches` gate's own canonicalizer — fixed here.
- Config model: the post-0.25 gates (`string_hazards`, `identical_branches`, `enum_name_contract`, `collapsible_flow`) are grouped into a `QualityGatesConfig` subgroup to keep the `GatesConfig` constructor under the `method_size` parameter cap. YAML keys are unchanged (still top-level `gates.string_hazards` etc. — no `quality` nesting in the file).

## 0.27.0 — 2026-10-29

- `reorder` now covers enum member sections: the constants block (enum value order — `values`, `.index`, ordinal persistence) is never touched, while fields, constructors, getters and methods after the constants are reordered into the canonical order exactly like a class body. Previously the entire enum body was skipped, so a constructor above its field survived in enhanced enums. Byte-identical for enums without a member section; constants are copied verbatim (spacing included), so `.index`/`values` semantics cannot drift.

## 0.26.0 — 2026-10-29

- New `enum_name_contract` gate (warning severity by default): flags usages of the built-in `.name`/`.index` members inside enum declaration bodies — the persisted YAML/JSON value changes when a Dart identifier is renamed (`Color.red.name` is `"red"` until the constant is renamed). Provable receivers only: `this`, implicit `this` (bare `name`/`index` in instance members without local shadowing), the enum's own constants, `values` loop variables and index accesses, and parameters explicitly typed with the enum. Self-shadowing (`name`/`index` members declared by the enum) is respected; usages outside enum bodies are out of scope. Fix hint: declare a `final String value` field and contract on `.value`. Dogfooded: the gate found and this release fixes the two shipped violations (`ComplexityMetric.tryParse`, `DuplicationReport.tryParse` — both now contract on an explicit `value` field).

## 0.25.0 — 2026-10-28

-

`memory` accepts positional test paths on the Flutter engine: `crap4dart memory test/foo_test.dart` measures that subset only (paths forward into both `flutter test` runs — targeted A/B without the whole-package cost). From a workspace root, the package root is inferred by walking up from the first path. Missing paths exit with a usage error naming them. Dart-engine behavior unchanged (paths already worked).

-

Adopt four additional lints on top of `lints/recommended` and fix all findings: `prefer_const_constructors` (55 sites, via `dart fix`), `unnecessary_ignore` (3 stale `// ignore:` comments removed — a stale ignore silently eats the next occurrence of the real diagnostic), `unnecessary_lambdas` and `use_string_buffers` (zero findings today; adopted for the shapes they prevent — callback over-wrapping and O(n²) string concatenation in loops).

## 0.24.0 — 2026-10-27

- New `identical_branches` gate (warning severity by default): the copy-paste-edit bug family, compared by canonical form (formatting-, parenthesis- and comment-independent; commutative operands sorted; same-operator nests flattened) — (1) duplicate conditions in one if/else-if chain, (2) duplicate branch bodies in one chain (including `else` equal to its `then`; a single-statement block equals the naked statement), (3) duplicate or absorbed operands in one boolean chain (`a || a` collapses to `a`; `a || b && a` collapses to `a` by absorption — the extra terms are dead), (4) identical ternary branches (`c ? x : x`), (5) duplicate positional arguments in one call (`f(w, h, w)`; named arguments exempt — the name documents the slot — and all-literal argument lists exempt, so uniform-value APIs like `EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(8, 8, 8, 8)` stay quiet), and (6) duplicate catch bodies in one try. Only pieces of the same construct are compared; identical conditions in separate `if` statements are legal. Config keys: `enabled`, `severity`, `ignorable`.
- `ConfigException` file-level failures no longer render the path in the key slot (`Invalid config "x": x: config file not found` → `Invalid config "x": config file not found`); the duplicate-argument finding that surfaced it came from the new gate's first dogfood run.

## 0.23.0 — 2026-10-27

- New `string_hazards` gate (warning severity by default): flags string literals whose escaping or pattern usage contradicts the author's almost-certain intent — (1) escaped interpolations (`\$name` / `\${name}` in non-raw strings render literally) flagged only when the same identifier is interpolated elsewhere in the file, (2) raw `RegExp` patterns ending with `\$` (or starting with `\^`) where the end/start anchor was intended, and (3) regex anchors (`^` / unescaped trailing `$`) inside literal `String` patterns of `replaceFirst`/`replaceAll`/`replace*Mapped`/`split`, where they can only match that literal character. Config keys: `enabled`, `severity`, `ignorable`.

## 0.22.0 — 2026-10-27

- New `reorder` command: deterministically rewrites class members into the canonical Dart/Flutter order (constants, static fields, fields, constructors, static methods, getters/setters, public methods, private methods — same-kind members keep their relative order; a stable partition, never alphabetical). Doc comments, annotations and `//` comment blocks directly above a member (even separated by one blank line) move with it; enum bodies are untouched; CRLF files keep their line endings. Idempotent and byte-stable on canonical input — including single-line class bodies and members sharing the header line, which are preserved (and never corrupted) as-is. `--dry-run` lists would-change files and exits 2 for CI/pre-commit use.
- Ignore comments gain Dart-lint-style granularity alongside the legacy `// crap:ignore` / `// crap:ignore-file` (both unchanged): `// ignore:<gate-id>` suppresses that gate on the line (trailing or stacked above — several markers combine), `// ignore-file:<id>` that gate file-wide. One rule per marker; `// ignore:` with no id means every ignorable gate; unknown ids are inert. The `ignorable: true` opt-in still applies per gate.
- `scattered_constants` — new `aliases` rule (default on): a private pure value alias (`const _x = kY;`) is flagged as adding a name without information; the message says to reference the shared constant directly. Public declarations (re-export shims) are exempt; `aliases: false` switches the rule off.
- `folder_structure` — `dirs` entries accept glob patterns (`lib/src/*`, `packages/**`) expanding to every matching directory, and generated siblings of one source file (`magic.dart` + `magic.g.dart` + `magic.freezed.dart`) count as one logical unit; only a directory's own files count (nested directories are the organized form). New optional `config` map with per-pattern caps — `config: {lib/src: 3, 'lib/src/**': 30}` — taking precedence over `dirs`/`max_loose_files`, which stay fully backward compatible.

## 0.21.0 — 2026-10-23

- `scattered_constants` v2: new constant-regression rule — when a named `const` for a value already exists in the corpus, every hardcoded re-introduction flags immediately (any occurrence count), naming the constant and its `file:line`; scattered literals (no constant, `min_files`+ files) keep the extract-and-verify message.
- `scattered_fragments` gate removed — too noisy in practice; parked on the `feature/scattered-constants-gate` branch (0.20.0) should we return to it.

## 0.19.0 — 2026-10-24

- Flutter memory reports no longer show a misleading `0.0` for reclaimed-new-gen churn: the VM Service GC stream has no reclaimed counters, so `churnNewMb` (per test/suite) and `totalChurnMb` are JSON `null` there, a top-level `churnAvailable` flag says so, and the console prints "new-gen churn unavailable". Use `allocatedMb` / `totalAllocatedMb` (exact allocated bytes) as the churn metric on both engines; `--badge` follows the same rule. Dart-engine output is unchanged (numeric churn, `churnAvailable: true`).

## 0.18.0 — 2026-10-23

- New `record_named_fields` gate: record type annotations with unnamed fields and `.$N` positional accesses are flagged.
- New `inline_record_types` gate: inline record types in signatures must move behind one named `typedef` declaration.
- New `record_size` gate: records over `max_fields` (default 5, positional plus named) should be transformed into classes.
- `PreparedRun` (CLI run preparation) converted from a six-field record typedef to a class — the first `record_size` dogfooding fix.

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

## Unreleased

### Added

- `identical_branches` gate (24th): fails `if`/`else if` chains that test the same condition twice — every later branch is unreachable, the copy-paste-edit bug family. Conditions compare by canonical form: whitespace-, parenthesis- and comment-independent, with operands of commutative operators sorted (`a == b` matches `b == a`) and `&&`/`||` nests flattened. Only conditions of one chain are compared (state may change between separate statements); `if case` links and `switch` are excluded. Enabled by default with `severity: warning` (reordering is only equivalent for side-effect-free operands).

### Fixed

- `gate_runner` ran `broken_goldens`, `test_assertions`, `folder_structure` and `external` twice per `check` (leftover from the external-gate commit); duplicate results are gone.

## 0.17.0 — 2026-10-23

### Added

- `memory --engine auto|dart|flutter` (default `auto`): Flutter test suites are now measurable. `auto` picks `flutter` when pubspec.yaml declares a `flutter:` dependency, else `dart`.

  - `flutter test` passes no VM flags through and the engine's `--dart-flags` whitelist rejects `--verbose_gc`; the Flutter mode instead re-runs every `flutter_tester` spawn traced by `flutter test --verbose --no-pub -j1 -r json` with the VM Service enabled, drives the suite over package:test's remote protocol (initial -> success -> run/close per test) and measures through the VM Service:

    - per-test ALLOCATED bytes — the allocation profile is reset before each test and read after it (exact, more precise than the Dart engine's reclaimed-new-gen proxy);
    - GC events from the `GC` stream, attributed by arrival;
    - old-gen growth chained across consecutive service events;
    - suite-load allocations read once before the first reset.

  - The tool deletes each file's temp dill when the file finishes and at -j1 outruns the measured copy: dills are snapshotted at trace time and the snapshots measured (and cleaned up after).
  - Every file executes twice (the tool's run plus the measured copy); trace paths must not contain commas (the tool prints its argv via plain `List.toString()`).

- Reports (both engines) gained `totalAllocatedMb` (JSON) and an `allocated` headline/column; the churn leaderboard sorts by allocation volume (Dart engine: reclaimed new-gen proxy; Flutter engine: profile-allocated bytes).

## 0.16.0 — 2026-10-22

### Added

- `memory` command (phase 1 of the memory-profiling plan): runs `dart --verbose_gc test --concurrency=1 -r json` and attributes GC events to tests — allocation churn (reclaimed new-gen MB, deterministic across runs) and old-gen growth (leak suspects). Per-test windows use each isolate's own clock (GC rows count from isolate start; the suite event time is the same zero); loading and teardown GCs land in an unattributed bucket. `--badge` writes a shields-style churn SVG (see `badges/memory.svg`).
- Dogfooding across three repos (file-level numbers stable across runs): crap4dart 497 tests / 245 MB (no heavy files — the earlier "30 MB" hotspots were detector artifacts, fixed by the window-only attribution); dmtools-dart 4254 tests / 1.5 GB (top: AiSyncTools transport test 35 MB, justified); flutter_agent 12387 tests / 84 GB (top: `AC3 — status without id stays bounded` 2.5 GB churn + 14.7 MB retained — reported upstream).

## 0.15.0 — 2026-10-15

### Added

- **`similarity` gate + `crap4dart similarity` command**: file-level near-duplicate detection over any text corpus — markdown docs, source files of any language, raw text. Copied docs that drifted apart, twin templates differing by a heading, stale snapshot copies, generated files duplicating their sources: each clustered file gets a violation naming its counterparts and the strongest pair metrics. 8-token shingles, Jaccard + containment thresholds, transitive clusters; markdown/code/raw normalization profiles (code fences, comments, import-family lines and literal values are normalized away). Opt-in (`enabled: false` by default) — explore with the informational `similarity` command, tune, then enforce, typically with a baseline so only new near-duplicates fail.
- **Native binary releases**: every `v*` tag now builds self-contained Linux x64/arm64 executables (`dart compile exe`, no Dart SDK needed at runtime) with SHA256 checksums attached to the GitHub release.

## 0.14.2 — 2026-10-15

### Fixed

- `broken_goldens` false positives against real-world goldens (measured on 187 current flutter_agent_harness goldens: 40 flagged before the fix, 1 documented residual after):

  - the tofu X must anchor its diagonals AT the box walls — the letter strokes inside a filled control (a white "S" on a Save button) also run a converge-merge-diverge cycle, but they start well inside the run and are now rejected;
  - hollow icon boxes must be RING-ISOLATED (the 2px ring around the box is pure background) — a copy icon's front panel has the rest of the glyph crossing it;
  - hollow icon boxes must have SQUARE corners and be 20-64 px — unchecked Material checkboxes are rounded 16-18 px squares;
  - solid glyph rectangles must have square corners — rows of rounded white dock/pagination tiles no longer read as Ahem text.

- `broken_goldens` measured on the 40 broken pre-font goldens from the flutter_agent_harness regression fixture: 30/40 detected (0/40 before 0.14.1); the residual 10 carry only sub-20 px boxes and the fa_mark logo (a real image).

## 0.14.1 — 2026-10-15

### Added

- `broken_goldens`: two new broken-golden shape classes (fixes blind spots from issue #3):

  - hollow icon boxes — a square-ish bordered box (14-64 px) with continuous walls and an empty interior, what an unloaded icon font actually draws (no diagonal cross needed);
  - solid glyph runs — at least two distinct solid rectangles of the same vertical extent side by side with a small gap (Ahem fallback text, a font that failed to load in the test environment).

- `gates.duplication` `report: clones`: the summary now also carries the project-wide duplicated-line percentage, so a number is always present regardless of the report mode.

### Fixed

- `broken_goldens` false positives (issue #4):

  - the tofu X now requires the full life cycle — diagonals converge, MERGE into one central band and then DIVERGE again. A checkmark V (green Habit-Tracker-style tiles) converges to its vertex and never re-diverges, so those tiles pass;
  - overflow stripes require the checkerboard's equal-length yellow/ black segments; amber digits on dark cards (4 px strokes on 7 px gaps) alternate but with unequal lengths and pass.

## 0.14.0 — 2026-10-12

### Added

- `gates.duplication`: PMD CPD parity, implemented natively (CPD itself has no Dart support):

  - `report: clones` — one violation per non-overlapping clone group (longest first), every occurrence location in the message; `percentage` stays the default.
  - `ignore_identifiers` — replace all identifiers with a placeholder before hashing (structure-only matching, CPD `--ignore-identifiers`); built-in/pseudo keywords included.
  - `ignore_imports` — exclude `import`/`export`/`part` directives from tokenization.
  - `skip_duplicate_files` — a file whose token stream equals an earlier file's is analyzed once (CPD `--skip-duplicate-files`).

### Fixed

- Duplication windows are now verified by actual token equality before reporting (Rabin-Karp fingerprint collisions no longer count as clones) and extended to the maximal extent the occurrences share.

## 0.13.0 — 2026-10-12

### Added

- `gates.complexity.metric`: `cyclomatic` (default) or `cognitive` — SonarSource-style cognitive complexity (flow breaks weighted by nesting depth; flat `else if` chains stay cheap, `&&`/`||` sequences count once per run). The CRAP score always uses cyclomatic complexity.

### Fixed

- Cyclomatic complexity now counts switch **expressions** (`return switch (x) { ... }`), their `when` guards, `if-case` guards, and `||`/`&&` patterns — previously all uncounted.
- The `nesting` gate no longer counts `else if` chains as nesting: a chained `if` keeps its originating `if`'s level, while an `if` inside an `else` block still adds one.

## 0.12.2 — 2026-10-11

### Added

- `mutation` gate: diff-scoped execution — under `--diff` / `--diff-base` only sites whose containing method intersects the changed lines are executed at all (sites outside the diff are neither executed nor counted), so a per-PR run pays only for the mutants of the changed methods.
- `mutation` gate: `scope_tests` (default false) — per-mutant test scoping to the derived test file(s) of the mutated file (`lib/src/foo/bar.dart` → `test/src/foo/bar_test.dart`, `test/foo/bar_test.dart`), falling back to `test_args` when no candidate exists. A scoped kill is monotone (the scoped invocation is a subset of the full suite) and is cached as a regular kill; a scoped survivor — a timeout included — is re-confirmed once against the full invocation, and only the confirmed outcome is reported and cached.

## 0.12.1 — 2026-10-11

### Fixed

- `mutation` gate integrity: a real run on a downstream project once ended with a leftover mutant on disk even though the per-site restore is `finally`-guarded (out-of-process defeat: external write or a killed VM between apply and restore). The engine now snapshots every file it will mutate before the loop and re-verifies the whole tree in an outer `finally`: any mismatch is re-restored and reported as `INTEGRITY: re-restored after run` in the summary plus a stderr warning, so silent tree corruption becomes a loud, self-healing error.

## 0.12.0 — 2026-10-11

### Added

- `mutation` gate hardening: digest-incremental killed-stays-killed cache. Per-method outcomes persist to `<projectRoot>/.crap-mutation-cache.json` (versioned envelope `{version, meta, methods}`) keyed by method identity (file + `className.methodName`) and an FNV-1a 64-bit digest of the method's exact AST source span (zero new dependencies). On later runs, covered mutants of unchanged methods with a matching site identity that were previously `killed` are replayed, not re-executed, and reported as `cached` in the summary; survivors always re-execute; changed/new methods re-execute fully; coverage gating is re-derived from fresh LCOV every run. The `meta` guard (tool version, operators, `test_args`) wipes the cache on mismatch; entries of vanished methods are pruned. New `gates.mutation` keys: `cache` (default true) and `test_args` (default `['test']` — full per-mutant test invocation args; strict validation: non-empty list of non-empty strings).
- `mutation` gate (22nd gate, disabled by default): mutation testing adapted from the unclebob/mutator research conclusions. A declarative category-tagged operator table (`arithmetic`, `boundary`, `equality`, `logical`, `boolean`, `constant`, `unary`) is matched on parsed ASTs (token offsets, never regex); covered sites are mutated one at a time and the test suite re-runs per mutant (non-zero exit kills — compile errors included; timeout counts as survived). Uncovered sites are excluded from the score. New `gates.mutation` keys: `min_score` (0.8), `max_survivors` (0), `timeout_seconds` (60), `max_mutants` (500), `operators` (all), `exclude` (generated + `test/**`), plus the standard `enabled`/`severity`/`ignorable`. One `GateViolation(file, line)` is reported per survived mutant, so diff mode and baselines work unchanged.

## 0.10.0 - 2026-09-28

### Added

- `duplication` gate: new `sources` key — additional file/directory paths (resolved against the project root) unioned into the duplication scan, enabling cross-module duplicate detection in monorepos without widening the CRAP analysis scope.

### Changed

- Dependencies refreshed: `analyzer` 7.3 -> 14.4 (new "parts" AST — `ClassDeclaration.namePart.typeName`, `NamedType.name`, `NamedArgument`/`Argument` model, `body.members`, `isComplete`), `xml` 7.1, `test` 1.32, `lints` 6.1.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2003): the Copilot picker filter is tier-aware. Individual-tier
  `/models` responses omit `model_picker_enabled` entirely, so phase 1
  dropped every such entry as «picker flag absent» and individual/OAuth
  accounts still listed zero usable models. When the response comes from
  the individual tier — the individual host (`api.githubcopilot.com` or
  pi-mono's `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` spelling) or a
  no-proxy-ep token (individual by design) — an ABSENT flag is now
  selectable: absence ≠ an explicit `false`, which still drops
  everywhere (embeddings, completion-only). Business/enterprise answers
  keep the strict picker list unchanged, and the keep is never silent:
  the fetch note names it («2 of 2 models kept via the individual-tier
  fallback (picker flag absent)») through the existing `fetch notes:`
  surfacing. pi-mono parity: the trigger mirrors `allowPolicyFallback =
  baseUrl === "https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com"` in
  `packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts`.

- name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 duplication gate.
          # crap4dart#3/#4 (2026-10-15): >=0.14.2 <0.15.0 — same bounded
          # pin as the core job; the broken_goldens detector fixes the
          # flipped configs rely on.
          # gh-1738: >=0.15.0 — same bounded pin as the core job; the
          # root config's similarity gate runs under this version.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.15.0 <0.16.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check
===
      # NEW duplication, same contract as CI.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --baseline; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — crap4dart gates" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      # Issue #1234 rework: the ≤2800 ceiling over test/ + example/ via
      # the loc-scope companion config (the package config's sources are
      # [lib, bin]; 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override). No-ops
      # unless a staged file lives under test/ or example/.
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart check --staged --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — loc scope (test/example)" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      ;;
    "")
      ;; # not activated — skip silently (CI and the fast gate cover it)
    *)
      echo "⚠️  crap4dart $C4D_VER is too old for the gates (need >= 0.15.0 — gh-1738 similarity keys);" \
           "skipping — run: dart pub global activate crap4dart '>=0.15.0 <0.16.0'" >&2
      ;;
  esac
fi

# Golden-coverage quick check — only when the staged diff can affect the
# flutter_app (the gate's own markers already told us the flutter stage
# ran or was skipped; recompute cheaply from the staged paths here).
STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only || true)
if echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '^(flutter_app/|packages/|lib/|scripts/|\.github/|pubspec\.)' \
   || ! echo "$STAGED" | grep -qE '\.(md)$|^docs/|^prompts/'; then
  if command -v flutter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🔍 Checking golden coverage..."
    if python3 scripts/check_goldens.py --quick; then
      echo "✅ Golden gate OK"
    else
      exit 1
    fi

# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).
if command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  C4D_VER=$(dart pub global list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="crap4dart"{print $2}')
  case "$C4D_VER" in
    # gh-1106: floor 0.11.0 — the root crap4dart.yaml duplication block
    # uses 0.11.0-only keys (ignore_locals/ignorable); the strict config
    # parser throws ConfigException on unknown keys, so older pins fail
    # rather than silently run without Type-2 detection.
    # gh-1738: floor 0.15.0 — the root config now carries the similarity
    # gate (gates.similarity); 0.11.0-0.14.x parsers ConfigException on
    # the unknown gate id, bricking every commit.
    0.1[5-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*|[1-9].*)
      echo "🧪 crap4dart gates (staged core files)..."
      # gh-1106: --baseline — the Type-2 duplication gate ships with a
      # committed snapshot of pre-existing findings; hooks must flag only
      # NEW duplication, same contract as CI.

🚨 **BLOCKING: `crap4dart.yaml` requires crap4dart ≥ 0.24.0, but every CI pin / pre-commit floor stays 0.15.x — the Quality-gates step throws `ConfigException` and fails CI**

The `identical_branches` gate was added in crap4dart **0.24.0** (config keys `enabled`/`severity`/`ignorable`), and the `// ignore:<gate-id>` marker channel in **0.22.0** (upstream CHANGELOG, pub.dev/GitHub, read this run). CI activates the pinned `>=0.15.0 <0.16.0` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1779`, "Activate crap4dart (pinned)") and runs `crap4dart check --baseline` in the *Quality gates* step (`ci.yml:1804`).

Reproduced with the exact pinned version on this branch:

```
$ dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.15.0 <0.16.0"   # → crap4dart 0.15.0
$ dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline
Invalid config ".../crap4dart.yaml": gates.identical_branches: unknown gate id
exit code 1
```

This is the exact failure mode the workflow's own pin-bump comments document ("unknown keys are a ConfigException", gh-1106) and the reason every prior gate addition bumped the pin **in the same PR** (gh-1106, crap4dart#3/#4, gh-1738). `scripts/pre-commit:63-96` has the same problem: its version floor `0.1[5-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*` lets 0.15–0.19 through, where `check --staged --baseline` throws the same `ConfigException` — every Dart-touching commit is bricked locally for devs on the documented floor.

**Fix (this PR):** bump the tool requirement to a gate-aware version in the same change, mirroring the gh-1738 pattern:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1779` → `dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.24.0 <0.26.0"` (or your chosen bounded pin) + the explanatory pin comment;
- `scripts/pre-commit` floor (`0.1[5-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*` case and the "need >= " message at line 93) → `>= 0.24.0`;
- for pin consistency, `ci.yml:2513` (flutter_app job uses the same constraint; its config is unaffected today, but keeping one bounded pin repo-wide is the established pattern).

Verified: with crap4dart **0.25.0** the same `check --baseline` run passes (exit 0; `identical_branches` + `loc` + `broken_goldens` + baselined `similarity` all green), so the bump is the only missing piece.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "26 → 0 violations" claim is off by one — one `identical_branches` violation survives its suppression marker**

With the tool version this PR was built against (crap4dart 0.25.0) and the `input/` scratch excluded, `dart pub global run crap4dart check --only identical_branches` still reports:

```
[WARN] identical_branches: 14 identical-branch findings (28230 constructs checked)
  lib/src/providers/conn_trace_bench_io.dart:436: duplicate catch body in try statement:
  '{_blameSendFailure(request.url, error...' (same as line 433)
```

The gate anchors this finding at line **436** (the `} on HttpException catch (error) {` clause), but the marker added here sits at line **437**, inside the body below the reported line — per the 0.22.0 marker contract (`// ignore:<gate-id>` suppresses **on the line, trailing or stacked above**), it never applies. The other 13 markers all suppress.

It stays invisible only because the gate is `severity: warning`; the moment `identical_branches` is escalated to `error` (the documented end-state for the `duplication` gate in this same file), CI goes red.

**Verified fix** (tested on this branch, then reverted): trail the marker on the clause line the tool reports —

```dart
} on HttpException catch (error) { // ignore:identical_branches — same blame+wrap as the SocketException arm.
```

→ `[PASS] identical_branches` (0 findings leak). Please apply that (or re-word to fit one trailing line) and re-run `crap4dart check --only identical_branches` so the "0 violations" gate claim in the PR description is true as committed.

💡 **SUGGESTION: breaking change to a barrel-exported constructor — add a `## Unreleased` changelog line**

`KaomojiFace` is exported from the public barrel (`lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart:166`), and this PR changes its constructor from four positional parameters to two positional + `{List<KaomojiRun>? fallbackRuns, required svg}`. Any external consumer constructing a face positionally stops compiling. The migration is correct and complete in-repo (all 8 faces + the `fa_ui` test caller verified, `flutter test test/fa_kaomoji_test.dart` → 10/10 green), and the `fallbackRuns ?? runs` default preserves values for the ASCII faces.

But the PR description says "no docs/changelog touched". The repo keeps a curated `## Unreleased` section in `CHANGELOG.md` exactly for noteworthy changes; a public-API signature change qualifies even for a tech-debt card. One line naming the old → new call shape (and that `svg` became required) spares downstream consumers a mystery compile error after their next `pub upgrade`.

(Non-blocking: `pubspec.yaml` is `0.0.0-dev`, so there is no semver gate to satisfy — this is documentation hygiene only.)

import subprocess
specs = [("crap4dart.yaml",152),("lib/src/providers/conn_trace_bench_io.dart",437),
         ("lib/src/kaomoji_faces.dart",31),("packages/fa_ui/test/fa_kaomoji_test.dart",379)]
for f, n in specs:
    diff = subprocess.run(["git","diff","origin/main...HEAD","-U0","--",f],
                          capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    in_hunk = False
    added = False
    for line in diff.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("@@"):
            parts = line.split()
            rng = parts[2]  # +start,count
            body = rng[1:]
            start = int(body.split(",")[0])
            count = int(body.split(",")[1]) if "," in body else 1
            in_hunk = start <= n < start + count
        elif in_hunk and line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"):
            if line[1:].rstrip() != "":
                # count which added line we're at
                pass
    # simpler: map added lines to their new-file line numbers directly
    added_lines = set()
    cur = None
    for line in diff.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("@@"):
            parts = line.split()
            body = parts[2][1:]
            cur = int(body.split(",")[0])
        elif cur is not None and line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"):
            added_lines.add(cur); cur += 1
        elif cur is not None and line.startswith("-"):
            pass
        elif cur is not None and (line.startswith(" ") or line==""):
            cur += 1
    print(f"{f}:{n}", "ADDED-LINE ✓" if n in added_lines else "NOT an added line ✗")
EOF
